title: A round that chooses a value
request:
three acceptors, a prepare to two of them, and then an accept to each

./your_program.sh paxos
init 3
prepare a1 1
prepare a2 1
accept a1 1 red
learn
accept a2 1 red
learn
note: Choosing is not something a proposer does; it is a fact about the acceptors that may be true before anybody has noticed. The proposer here never learns the outcome — a separate learner has to go and look, which is why `learn` is a command of its own.

title: A proposer forced to abandon its value
request:
a proposer that wants `blue`, and two promises, the second reporting `red`

./your_program.sh paxos
init 3
accept a1 2 red
propose 5 blue
promise a2 -1 -
promise a1 2 red
proposer
note: This one rule is the whole of Paxos safety. A proposer that keeps its own value, or that keeps whichever promise arrived last, can choose a second value for a decree that was already decided — and nothing downstream will ever notice, because both rounds look perfectly legal from the outside.

title: Two proposers preempting each other
request:
one proposer's prepares, a rival's higher prepares, then the first's accepts

./your_program.sh paxos
init 3
prepare a1 1
prepare a2 1
prepare a1 2
prepare a2 2
accept a1 1 red
accept a2 1 red
learn
note: Repeat this and neither proposer ever finishes: Paxos is safe under duelling proposers but not live. The cure is a distinguished proposer, which is exactly what Multi-Paxos and Raft both build in.
